symbols.name: Evidence
symbols.note: Dataclass holding evidence paths and file contents. refs() produces citations with digest of exact bytes; text_tokens() sums token counts; from_patch_artifact and from_files constructors.

symbols.name: Evidence.refs
symbols.note: Returns tuple of evidence_ref(path, sha256 of utf-8 bytes of text) for each file.

symbols.name: Evidence.text_tokens
symbols.note: Returns sum of count_tokens for each file's text.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_patch_artifact
symbols.note: Classmethod building Evidence from a PatchArtifact-like object; uses getattr to tolerate missing attributes.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_files
symbols.note: Classmethod reading files from disk; unreadable files are represented as placeholder text naming the exception type.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_text
symbols.note: Classmethod building Evidence from a single text string.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing one verbatim claim by a participant; has checkable flag and check string.

symbols.name: TurnRef
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing one chained turn with status, reason, content, and metadata flags.

symbols.name: ParticipantRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for roster accounting; includes outcome, reason, withheld, rounds_spoken, operator_trusted.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for the council's advisory output. Enforces advisory=True in __post_init__. Provides derived views: checkable_claims, quorum, claims_by_author, render.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.__post_init__
symbols.note: Validates advisory is True and ended is in END_REASONS.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.checkable_claims
symbols.note: Returns tuple of claims where checkable is True.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.quorum
symbols.note: Returns a formatted string of responded/requested and distinct weight families.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.claims_by_author
symbols.note: Returns dict of author to tuple of claims, sorted by author.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.render
symbols.note: Returns a human-readable string representation of the council record.

symbols.name: _parse_claims
symbols.note: Parses response content into Claim tuples. If no claim markers found, returns a single parsed=False claim (truncated in this chunk).

claims.text: Evidence citations: path + sha256 of the EXACT bytes shown.
claims.why: refs() computes evidence_ref(path, (text or '').encode('utf-8', 'replace')) for each file, so the digest is over the exact bytes shown.

claims.text: Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without the digest the transcript records a citation nobody can reproduce.
claims.why: The code includes a digest in the ref, which allows reproduction; the rationale is consistent.

claims.text: ``changed_paths`` becomes the path channel; the diff itself is shown as one evidence file so the content channel scans it whole-file, per the floor's own contract.
claims.why: from_patch_artifact sets paths from artifact.changed_paths and files to a single ('PATCH.diff', diff) entry.

claims.text: Read files off disk as evidence. Unreadable files are NAMED, never silently dropped -- a missing evidence file that reads as an empty one is a council reviewing something other than what it says it reviewed.
claims.why: The try/except appends a placeholder string naming the exception type when read_text raises OSError, so the file is named and not silently empty.

claims.text: ``checkable`` is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion.
claims.why: The Claim dataclass has the field, but the logic that sets checkable is in _parse_claims, which is truncated in this chunk.

claims.text: A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own.
claims.why: The recording of non-checkable claims is in _parse_claims, truncated here; this chunk only shows the Claim dataclass.

claims.text: The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing.
claims.why: The dataclass has advisory: bool = True and __post_init__ raises if advisory is not True, and render() states it is advisory.

claims.text: There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object.
claims.why: The fields listed in the dataclass contain no such decision fields; __post_init__ enforces advisory=True.

claims.text: Secret-floor rule LABEL that refused the outbound call, never the bytes.
claims.why: The field is typed str and the comment states it holds a label, not bytes.

claims.text: Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision.
claims.why: __post_init__ raises if advisory is not True, enforcing the invariant.

claims.text: The queue the gate can actually run.
claims.why: The property filters claims by c.checkable, which is the deterministic check flag.

claims.text: ``"2 of 4 (2 distinct weight families)"`` -- never a bare fraction. "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same thing.
claims.why: The property returns a string with both the fraction and the distinct weight family count, so they cannot be confused.

claims.text: Human rendering. The degraded flag sits ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS -- never in a footer, where a reader takes a two-vendor council for four.
claims.why: In render(), the degraded flag is appended to the quorum line, which is near the top with the findings, not in a footer.

observations.what: Evidence.from_files uses errors='replace' when reading, so invalid UTF-8 bytes are replaced with U+FFFD; the digest in refs() is computed over the replaced bytes, not the original bytes on disk. The docstring says 'EXACT bytes shown', which is accurate for the shown bytes but not the original file bytes.

Evidence.from_patch_artifact sets digest from artifact.diff_sha256, but refs() computes the digest from the actual diff text. If the artifact's diff_sha256 is stale or computed differently, the evidence_refs digest may not match the digest field.
CouncilRecord.quorum uses 'weight family/families' which is grammatically awkward; the docstring example uses 'weight families'.
CouncilRecord.__post_init__ validates ended against END_REASONS, but END_REASONS is defined elsewhere; this chunk cannot verify that all end reasons are covered.
_parse_claims is truncated; the full logic for setting parsed=False and checkable is not visible, so several claims about Claim behavior are uncheckable.
